context.title: Skin Diseases
context.summary: Priests are told how to examine skin conditions and decide whether a person is clean or unclean, with periods of isolation; the chapter ends with similar rules for mold in garments.
context.background: The Hebrew word translated 'leprosy' covers a range of skin conditions, and even mold on cloth or walls; it is not the same as modern leprosy (Hansen's disease). The priest acted as an inspector deciding fitness for community worship, not as a physician offering treatment.

customs.note: The person wore torn clothes, left the hair loose, covered the upper lip and called out a warning, then lived apart outside the camp, signs that also resembled mourning.

watchFor: The priest 'shall look' again and again: careful observation, not guesswork.
Waiting periods of seven days before a decision (vv. 4–6).

people.name: Moses
people.summary: Drawn (or Egypt. mesu, “son;” hence Rameses, royal son). On the invitation of Pharaoh (Gen. 45:17-25), Jacob and his sons went down into Egypt.

people.name: Aaron
people.summary: The eldest son of Amram and Jochebed, a daughter of Levi (Ex. 6:20). Some explain the name as meaning mountaineer, others mountain of strength, illuminator.
